extracted.intended_audience: readers of political economy and national finance (policymakers, informed public, critics of economic pamphlets)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging the state of a nation's finances and balance of trade, and for evaluating economic/political arguments about them. Includes what counts as reliable trade data, how to measure taxation burden, and how to judge assertions about national prosperity or decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inaccuracy of custom-house entries limited to free goods
rubrics_metrics.description: The inaccuracy of these entries can extend only to FREE GOODS, that is, to such British products and manufactures, as are exported without drawback and without bounty; which do not in general amount to more than two thirds at the very utmost of the whole export even of our home products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable articles like corn, malt, leather, hops, beer are not affected by this inaccuracy; therefore one cannot make a general defalcation from the whole balance in our favor based on entry errors that concern only free goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate (drawback) goods entries are reliable
rubrics_metrics.description: The article of CERTIFICATE GOODS re-exported, a vast branch of our commerce, admits of no error, (except some smaller frauds which cannot be estimated,) as they have all a drawback of duty, and the exporter must therefore correctly specify their quantity and kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because drawbacked/exported goods require specification for duty purpose, their export entries should be treated as accurate when assessing trade balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector-General's accounts use original cost only
rubrics_metrics.description: In the account made up at the Inspector-General's office, they estimate only the original cost of British products as they are here purchased; and on foreign goods, only the prices in the country from whence they are sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method omits the merchant's domestic profits and factory profits abroad; an allowance (e.g., about five per cent overall) should be added to reflect these omitted profits when assessing real export value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include shipping costs/employment as part of trade value
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not comprehend the advantage arising from the employment of 600,000 tons of shipping, which must be paid by the foreign consumer, and which, in many bulky articles of commerce, is equal to the value of the commodity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shipping charges paid by foreign consumers can materially increase the effective value derived from exports and should be estimated (here suggested scarcely less than a million annually) when judging trade advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat colonial and Irish imports as domestic/home trade
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole import from Ireland and America, and from the West Indies, is set against us in the ordinary way of striking a balance of imports and exports; whereas the import and export are both our own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting these flows as foreign trade is misleading — they are essentially home trade for national profit; examine the course of exchange to see where final profit accrues rather than raw entry figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Custom-house entries understate Newfoundland trade value
rubrics_metrics.description: The custom-house entries furnish a most defective, and, indeed, ridiculous idea of the most valuable branch of trade we have in the world,--that with Newfoundland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exports to Newfoundland (small provisions and supplies) and imports (food) are both 'our own' in effect; the true measure is the sale in foreign markets where Newfoundland produce is shipped — this trade may be worth ~400,000_l._ annually though it shows little in entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider quality (materials) of imports, not just quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of your imports must be considered as well as the quantity. ... iron, hemp, flax, cotton, Spanish wool, raw silk, woollen and linen-yarn ... are materials of industry, not of luxury, which are wrought up here, in many instances, to ten times, and more, of their original value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat raw-material imports as contributions to internal wealth and productive capacity rather than mere luxury consumption; this transforms how imports affect national advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use averages rather than accidents when judging prices
rubrics_metrics.description: Take average and not accident, the grand and first necessary of life is cheap in this country; and that too as weighed, not against labor ... but against money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not base claims of general dear living on temporary bad harvests or particular high-price episodes; examine average prices and compare against wages/money supply to judge real burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three standards for judging good condition of national finances
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three standards to judge of the good condition of a nation with regard to its finances. 1st, The relief of the people. 2nd, The equality of supplies to establishments. 3rd, The state of public credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any assessment of a nation's financial health should evaluate (1) the tax burden and relief to the populace, (2) whether supplies/revenues fairly match state expenditures/establishments, and (3) the quality and stability of public credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge distress by interest burden rather than principal alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Everybody knows that the principal of the debt is but a name; the interest is the only thing which can distress a nation. Take this idea ... and compare the interest paid by France with that paid by England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative tables of interest payments (and funds prices) are more informative about fiscal distress than headline debt figures; include funded and unfunded interest obligations and market valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish borrowing from supplies 'raised within the year'
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact is this: the credit of France, bad as it might have been, did enable her (not to raise within the year) but to borrow the very sums the author mentions; that is to say ... The author mistook the identical sums borrowed by France upon interest, for supplies raised within the year!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate borrowing (debt accumulation) with annual revenues raised; an author's failure to distinguish these leads to gross mischaracterisation of fiscal capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assuming or inventing facts to support a theory
rubrics_metrics.description: In general this author is so circumstanced, that to support his theory he is obliged to assume his facts: and then, if you allow his facts, they will not support his conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments about national condition must be grounded in probative evidence and transparent methods; do not 'assume facts' or beg the question to drive conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer methodical comparison and explanation of estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: One would have thought the natural method in a plan of reformation would be, to take the present existing estimates as they stand; and then to show what may be practicably and safely defalcated from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing new peace/establishment estimates or reforms, first take current estimates and give reasons for each proposed increase or cut; avoid ad hoc or unreasoned re-estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for wartime/peacetime market shifts when comparing trade
rubrics_metrics.description: It is true, that whilst the impressions of the author's destructive war continued, our trade was greater than it is at present. One of the necessary consequences of the peace was, that France must gradually recover a part of those markets ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that war temporarily alters trade flows and that peace can restore competitors' markets; compare comparable periods (e.g., best years before increase of debt/taxes vs last years) rather than mixing wartime peaks with peacetime baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider internal manufacturing and consumption indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: When a representation is built on truth and nature, one member supports the other ... as our manufacturers have not deserted, nor the manufacture left us, nor the consumption declined, nor the revenue sunk; so neither has trade ... in the least decayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manufacturing retention, domestic consumption, and revenue trends as corroborating indicators of trade health rather than relying solely on selective balance figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare taxation burden relative to country wealth and other nations
rubrics_metrics.description: I am fairly warranted to assert, that England is the most lightly taxed of any of the great states of Europe. ... I say ... that her subjects pay more than England, on a computation of the wealth of both countries; that her taxes are more injudiciously and more oppressively imposed; more vexatiously collected ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tax systems by burden relative to national wealth and by incidence/collective effects (e.g., excises on food in other countries, capitation, feudal charges) rather than nominal rates alone.
